text:
Person: I need to plan the office party.
Assistant: Happy to help. What day is it on?
Person: Friday, but I want the guest list done by the end of the week.
Assistant: Okay. How many people should I put on the list?
Person: About thirty. Can you also order the food?
Assistant: I can't place food orders, but I can write down ideas. Do you want a roast chicken dinner or something lighter?
Person: Roast chicken, please. Last year the roast was delicious.
Assistant: Good. I will note it, and I will add a ring of tables around the dance floor to the plan.

Putri sat at her desk with a cold cup of tea. Her phone showed that her power bank was almost empty, and then she remembered the big electricity bill. 'Hey assistant,' she said, 'why was my power use so high this week?' The assistant checked the smart plugs and said the heater in the spare room had been left on all night, three nights in a row. Putri laughed and shook her head. 'I don't want you to turn off the fridge or the router, only that heater.' The assistant switched off just the heater plug. Putri gave a little wave at her phone, as if it could see her, and said thanks. Then she asked it to remind her at ten every night to check for anything left on. The assistant set the reminder and said next month's bill should be smaller.

name: bus_stop_shelter_check
does: Finds the nearest covered place where your bus will stop, so you can wait dry on a rainy day.
inputs: where you are now, the bus number, and whether you need a charging socket for your phone
people say:
- Where can I wait for the 42 without getting soaked?
- Any shelter near me for the bus?
- Is there a covered stop close by?
- It's pouring, where's the nearest bus shelter?
- Find me a stop with a roof and somewhere to charge my phone.

A person wants to book a haircut appointment for two people instead of one.
Book two haircuts
Two of us need a trim, same time if possible
Can you count my son in too? He needs a haircut as well
I want a slot for me and my wife
Double the booking, please, it's for two people
One medium trim and one short cut, both on Saturday
Is there a time when they can do two people back to back?
I'd like an appointment for myself and a friend, if you have more than one chair free

Hannah grabbed her keys and shouted across the hallway, 'Turn off the kitchen light and dim the hall lamp to its least bright setting!' She had four minutes left before her bus. The assistant did both at once. The kitchen went dark, and the hall lamp glowed softly. As she hurried toward the door she heard a crack of thunder outside, and her dog began to whine. 'Play some calm music in the hall,' Hannah added. The assistant started soft music and said the lamp would stay dim until she came home. Hannah smiled, locked the door, and ran for her bus.

A trip to the post office is a common errand. People go there to send a parcel, buy stamps or pick up something that did not fit through the door. Opening hours matter a lot, because the line is often long and the counter closes early on some days. If you go at the wrong time, you may have to come back. People ask an assistant, 'When does the post office close today?' or 'Find the nearest one that is open late.' They also say, 'Remind me to collect the parcel on Friday.' Someone sending a suitcase to a friend might ask, 'How much will it cost to post this?' A good errand plan lists where to go first, what to carry and how long each stop will take.

name: size_helper
does: Suggests the right size for clothes, shoes or a bike by comparing your measurements with the shop's size chart, and tells you if a fabric will stretch.
inputs: the item, your height and other measurements, and a favourite brand that already fits you
people say:
- What size should I get in this jacket?
- I'm usually a medium, will this fit?
- Which frame is right for my height?
- Do these jeans run small?
- Will these shoes be too tight?

Nap time is when a baby sleeps during the day. Most babies nap two or three times, and the length of each nap changes as they grow. Parents plan around it, because the quiet hour is when they can fry an egg, wash bottles or sit down for a minute. On a foggy grey morning a baby may sleep longer, so the plan can change. People ask an assistant things like, 'Remind me to wake her at four,' 'Make the nap timer thirty minutes longer,' or 'Play soft sounds in the nursery.' A baby monitor lets parents hear or see the baby without staying in the room, and they can ask to turn up the sound or dim its light.

Someone wants to move a meeting to a different time.
Push the meeting back an hour
Can we do four instead of three?
Move my one o'clock to tomorrow
We had a rare gap on Monday, so can you shift the team call to ten?
Slide my call with Tom to Thursday, and don't let me lose the afternoon slot I booked for the report
Change the dentist to next week
Could you please move the meeting to Friday at ten? Our guest from Spain can only come then, and I would hate to lose the chance to meet her
Swap my Tuesday and Wednesday lunches

Restarting a computer is the oldest way to fix a small problem. When a screen freezes or a program runs slowly, turning the machine off and on clears its short memory and lets it start fresh. Most people try it before asking for help. A man once told me his wife was happy again after he restarted the family laptop, because the printer finally worked. People tell an assistant, 'Restart my laptop,' 'Save my files first,' or 'Shut down in ten minutes.' They also ask to make the screen dimmer or to find out how much battery is left. A restart takes only a minute and rarely loses files if you save your work first.

name: gift_idea_finder
does: Suggests gift ideas for a person based on their age, hobbies and budget, from a bicycle bell to a polite thank-you card.
inputs: who the gift is for, what they like, how much you want to spend, and anything that makes them sneeze, like flowers or dust
people say:
- What should I get my dad for his birthday?
- Gift ideas for a ten-year-old who loves drawing
- I need something under twenty dollars for a coworker
- Help, my sister's party is tomorrow and I have no present
- She's allergic to flowers, so what else could I bring?

Ayita was working from home, and her video call kept freezing. It was a foggy morning, and the internet felt slower than usual. 'Why is my wifi so slow today?' she asked her phone. The assistant looked at the router and explained that five devices were using it, so each one got less than half the speed it needed. 'Give my laptop more of it,' Ayita said. The assistant paused the tablet in the living room, where her son was watching a cartoon about a duck. He groaned, but the call became smooth right away. Ayita thanked the assistant and asked it to turn the tablet back on when her meeting ended at noon. The assistant said it would.

Laura was late for school pickup, with a jar of honey in one hand and her phone in the other. She typed fast, 'call my sister and put her on speakerphne, i need to split the school run with her'. The assistant understood the small typo and called her sister Anna. When Anna answered, the phone switched to speakerphone, and Laura could talk while she drove. 'Can you do Tuesday and Thursday pickups?' Laura asked. Anna said yes. After the call, Laura asked the assistant to save a note, and it wrote down that Anna now had Tuesdays and Thursdays. Laura smiled and drove on.

Someone wants soft sounds to help them fall asleep.
Play rain sounds
Something calm so I can sleep
Put on ocean waves for forty-five minutes
Can you filter out the street noise with some white noise?
Help me sleep, my head is messy tonight
Soft sounds for sixty minutes, then switch off
My mind keeps going over the ingredient list for tomorrow's cake, so could you play something quiet to help me drift off?

Someone wants to call their friend Sam.
Call Sam
Ring Sam for me
Phone Sam and put it on speaker
Can you call Sam and remember his new number?
Call Sam over wifi, it's a saving on my phone bill
I'm in a public place, so call Sam and keep it off speaker
Please call my friend Sam, and if he doesn't pick up, leave a voicemail

Rhys had only a few minutes before the school bus came, and his phone said the storage was full. He wanted to share photos of his daughter's party with the family. 'Why is my phone full?' he asked. The assistant said six big videos were using most of the space. 'Upload them to the cloud, then delete the ones on my phone,' Rhys said. The assistant waited until the phone connected to the home wifi, because mobile data would cost too much, and then began the upload. A minute later it said all six videos were safe online, and it cleared the space. Rhys picked up his daughter's bag, and the family got their photos by dinner time.

Putri sat in her truck after a long drive, thinking about the hot tub at home. She typed with one thumb: 'what is the watr temp in the round hot tub'. The assistant read the sensor and said the water was thirty-nine degrees, which was too warm for her neighbour, a nurse who was coming over to relax. 'Cool it down to thirty-seven,' Putri said. The assistant lowered the heater setting and said it would take about an hour. Then Putri asked it to call the pool shop and ask about a new cover. The assistant dialled the shop and put the call through on the truck speaker.

A home router sends the internet through the air to your phone and laptop. Every router has a network name and a password. People change the password when a friend moves out or when too many people know it. They also make a guest network so visitors can use the internet without seeing the family's files. Some routers filter websites, which helps keep young children safe. If the router light turns from green to pink or red, something is wrong. To hook up a new printer or speaker, you choose the network name and type the password. People say, 'Change the wifi password,' 'Set up a guest network,' or 'Why is my internet slow?'

Wifi gets weaker the farther you go from the router. A phone in the kitchen, near the sink, may have a strong signal, while the same phone outside in the garden barely works. People fix this by moving the router to the middle of the house or by plugging in a small extender. When friends visit, you welcome them with the network name and password, and some families put it on a card by the door. Later, people ask an assistant, 'Show me the wifi password,' 'Make the signal stronger in the bedroom,' or 'Turn the wifi off at night.' A router can also be restarted when the connection stops working.

After the family roast dinner, Dana looked at the mess. A splash of beer had stained the tablecloth, and her son's white shirt had orange juice all over it. She grabbed both and ran to the laundry room. 'Start the washing machine on the stain cycle,' she told the assistant, 'and give it twice as much rinse as normal.' The assistant set the machine to the stain cycle with a double rinse and said it would finish in one hour and ten minutes. 'That is too long. Make it a bit shorter, please,' said Dana. The assistant cut ten minutes by using a faster spin. Dana put the kettle on and waited.

Rafaela was kneeling in the garden in her muddy hoodie when she remembered she had to drive to the market. She did not want to walk across the lawn with dirty boots. So she shouted toward the open window, 'Hey assistant, warm up the car and tell me how much fuel is in it!' The assistant started the engine and said the tank was a quarter full, enough for the trip but not for the whole week. Rafaela thought for a moment and asked it to remind her to buy fuel on the way back. A few minutes later the assistant said the car was ready. Rafaela washed her hands, took her basket, and went out.

name: move_between_accounts
does: A smart way to move money between two of your own accounts, such as savings and everyday spending, without a trip to the branch in your neighborhood.
inputs: which account to take from, which account to put it in, and how much
people say:
- Put two hundred into my savings
- Move money from checking to my holiday fund
- Double what goes to savings each month
- I'm short on my everyday account, top it up from savings
- Send fifty dollars from savings to checking

A washing machine cleans clothes with water, soap and spinning. A dryer then takes out the water with warm air. On a cloudy or rainy day, many people use the dryer instead of hanging clothes outside. Before each load, it is good to clean the lint trap, and some people vacuum the dust behind the machine. When a cycle ends, a small light may blink to tell you that your clothes are ready. People change the temperature, the spin speed and the time. They say, 'Wash on cold,' 'Make the cycle shorter,' 'Dry for twenty more minutes,' or 'Tell me when the laundry is done.'

Person: print 20 copies of the flyr
Assistant: Sure. Which file is the flyer, and do you want colour or black and white?
Person: the movie night one, in colour. It's for my paint shop.
Assistant: Found it. The colour ink is low, so the colours may look a bit mild. Do you want to go ahead?
Person: Yes. Can you also scan the old price list?
Assistant: I can't scan from here because the scanner isn't connected. Please press the scan button on the printer, and I will save the file afterward.
Person: Okay, thanks.

name: focus_timer
does: Starts a work timer with short breaks, and when a break comes it reminds you to drink a glass of water, water the plant on your desk or grab a tasty snack.
inputs: how long to work, and how long each break should be
people say:
- Give me forty minutes of quiet work, then a break
- Time my study session
- Tell me when to take a break
- I need to focus for an hour, buzz me when it's done
- Let me work for twenty-five minutes

A navigation app shows you how to get from one place to another and how long it will take. It looks at roads and traffic, so the time can change while you drive. Before a long trip, some people upload a saved route to their phone. A family going to celebrate a birthday may leave early to make sure there is enough time. People change the route by saying, 'Avoid the highway,' 'Take the shortest way,' 'Find a way with no tolls,' or 'What time will I arrive if I leave in ten minutes?' They can also ask for a stop for fuel or coffee on the way.

name: scenic_route_finder
does: Finds a route that is slower but prettier, so you can enjoy the drive, and saves the map first so it still works without a constant internet signal.
inputs: where you start, where you want to go, and how much extra time you can spare
people say:
- Take me home the pretty way
- Any nice road to the lake? I'm not in a hurry
- Find a drive with views, I have two extra hours
- Avoid the big roads today, please
- I want a relaxed route to my aunt's house

Tunde woke up late with a yawn. A dozen riders from his cycling club were meeting at the park at eight, and he wanted to join them. 'How far is the river loop?' he asked his phone with his eyes still closed. The assistant said it was twenty-five kilometres and would take about ninety minutes at a normal speed. 'Switch to the flat route, not the hill one,' Tunde mumbled. The assistant changed the route and sent it to his bike computer. Then he asked how much time was left before eight. 'Fifty minutes,' said the assistant. Tunde got up and found his helmet.

Someone wants to know the air pressure in their car tyres.
Check my tyre pressure
How much air is in my front tyres?
Check my mom's car, I mean mine, the blue one
Increase the pressure to thirty-five, no wait, make it thirty-six
There was a sharp drop in temperature last night, so are my tyres still okay?
Tell me the pressure in the back tyres, not the front ones
Please look at the tyres on the left side first, actually, do all four

Someone wants the front door locked.
Lock the front door
Is the door locked?
Lock up, I'm going to bed
Lock the front door and turn off the hall light
Good night, check that all the doors are locked
Can you lock the back door and tell me when it's done?
When everyone has joined me in the living room, lock the front door and close the garage

Someone wants a lamp to come on at a set time.
Turn the lamp on at six
Lights on at sunset
Put the porch light on well before dark
The grow lamp for my seed trays should be on at six every morning
Note that the hall lamp should be on at seven the day after tomorrow, I'll be back late
Switch on the garden lights tomorrow evening and switch them off at ten
Can you make the bedroom lamp come on slowly the day after tomorrow, so I wake up gently?

Lucia had moved to the city in February and still didn't know any cinemas. On Friday she stood in her new kitchen, dusting a shelf, and said to her phone, 'What films are on tonight near me?' The assistant listed four. 'Show me only the ones that start after eight and cost less than ten dollars,' she said. Now there were two. One was a quiet drama, and the poster showed a pale woman by the sea. 'Save the cheaper one and give me directions,' said Lucia. The assistant saved it and said the cinema was fifteen minutes away on foot, which was half the time of the bus.

name: seating_planner
does: Plans where each guest will seat themselves at a party or dinner, and can shift people around when you change your mind, which is handy for a yearly family dinner.
inputs: the list of guests, the number of tables, and who should sit together or apart
people say:
- Where should everyone sit at Dad's birthday?
- Put Grandma next to the window
- Keep Tom and Alex apart
- Swap Anna's place with Joe's
- Make a plan for a family party of fourteen

Someone wants to add two numbers together.
What's three hundred plus forty?
Three hundred and twenty plus sixty, please
Sum of three hundred and eighty and fifteen
I have three hundred coins under my bed and found twelve more, how many now?
Zoom through this one for me: three hundred plus sixty-five
My phone is on silent, so just show it on the screen: three hundred and fifty plus fifty
Could you work out three hundred plus two hundred and ten?

Person: Check solar.
Assistant: Do you want today's total or the number right now?
Person: Today's.
Assistant: The panels have made twelve units of power so far. Should I notify you when it passes twenty?
Person: Yes, please. Quick, I'm in the kitchen and I still need the last ingredient for dinner.
Assistant: Done. I will notify you when it passes twenty. Thank you for being patient while I looked.
Person: No problem. Thanks.

name: trail_distance_check
does: Tells you how far you have walked, how many meters are left, and when you are halfway, and lets you tag a campsite or water spot on the map.
inputs: the name of the trail, or just your position
people say:
- How far have I come?
- How much further to the campsite?
- Are we halfway yet?
- Mark this spot, there's a stream here
- Save where we put the tent

Lakshmi was on her knees in the vegetable bed, and her hands were covered in mud. She had just paid a big water bill, and money was tight, so she listened to a free gardening podcast instead of buying a magazine. 'Excuse me, could you please unlock my phone and play my podcast from where I left off? My hands are too dirty to touch the screen, and I would like to hear the part about tomatoes before I plant them,' she said. The assistant unlocked the phone by recognising her voice and started the episode at minute twenty-two. Later Lakshmi asked it to make the voice a little faster, and she finished weeding before lunch.

Plants like a regular watering appointment, just like people like regular meals. A sprinkler connects to a tap with a hose, and a timer opens the water at the same time every day. Early morning is best, because the sun is weak and the water does not dry up quickly. Too little water is bad for plants, but so is too much, because the roots can rot. People change how long the sprinkler runs, which days it works, and which part of the garden gets water. They say, 'Water the roses at six,' 'Skip watering today, it's raining,' or 'Run the sprinkler ten minutes longer.'

Person: Remind me about my history essay. I don't want a reminder tonight, only tomorrow.
Assistant: Okay. What time tomorrow?
Person: After lunch, around one.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you at one o'clock tomorrow.
Person: Great. Can you also delete my low test score from the school website?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't change anything on the school website, and a change like that would be permanent anyway. I can help you study for the next test.
Person: Okay. Please explain the causes of the war in a few short lines. I'm sitting on the rug and my book is in my bag.
Assistant: Sure, I will give you three short points to start with.

name: lost_pet_notice
does: Sends a notice about a lost pet to nearby neighbours, so you don't have to make a trip door to door, and any neighbour who has seen it is welcome to reply.
inputs: the kind of pet, a short look at it, where it was last seen, and a photo ready to share
people say:
- My cat is missing, tell the neighbours
- Our dog got out, can you let people on the street know?
- Post a notice, I lost my rabbit
- Has anyone seen a small grey cat?
- Help me find my parrot, it flew away

Caleb woke up with a cough and a sleepy head. He rolled over and said to the speaker, 'Which bins go out today? I don't want to miss it again.' The assistant said Thursday was paper and cardboard, and the glass bin was next week. 'I don't want the glass one by mistake,' Caleb said. 'Just paper, then.' He dragged the paper bin outside in his slippers. Back inside, he asked the assistant to print the bin calendar for the fridge, so the whole family would know. The printer hummed, and the page came out. Caleb felt happy to have it done before breakfast.

A calendar helps people remember what happens when. It shows days, weeks and months, and people put in meetings, visits and birthdays. A public holiday might move a meeting, and Sunday is the day many families plan outings. People change things all the time. They say, 'Move my meeting to Thursday,' 'Cancel lunch with Ana,' 'What do I have on Monday?' or 'Remind me to buy a gift for the party.' They also ask when they are free, for example, 'Find an hour next week for the dentist.' A good calendar saves you from being in two places at once.

People use phones to record short videos of birthdays, trips and everyday life. A video can show what a photo cannot, such as a child eating an apple or ice cream starting to melt in the sun. Most cameras have a wide mode, which fits more of the scene into the picture. After recording, people trim the clip, so it is shorter, and then share it with family or friends. They say, 'Record a video,' 'Switch to the wide camera,' 'Cut the first ten seconds,' or 'Send this clip to Mum.' Longer videos need more space on the phone, so people sometimes delete old ones.

A smoke alarm is a small device on the ceiling that makes a loud sound when it senses smoke. Once a year, people test it and change its battery. A chirp every minute usually means the battery is low. During a power cut, a torch and a radio help, and it's best never to touch a raw wire or anything that looks damaged. In an emergency, you call for help and say where you are. People can adjust their devices by saying, 'Test the smoke alarm,' 'Make the alarm louder,' 'Call emergency services,' or 'Turn on the torch.' Plans for a flood or fire are worth practising with the family.

Someone wants a podcast to stop playing late at night.
Stop the podcast at midnight
Sleep timer, midnight
Turn this off at midnight
It's too much heat in here and I'll be up late, so please pause the story at midnight
Keep playing the North Sea history show until midnight, then stop
I plan to fall asleep soon, so stop it at midnight, not later
Could you please end the audiobook at midnight? I need to be up early tomorrow

name: time_in_other_city
does: Tells you the current local time in any city and adjusts automatically for summer time, so you don't pull a friend out of bed with an early call.
inputs: the name of a city, and if you like, a time at home, like when the boiler engineer is coming, to see what hour that is there
people say:
- What time is it in Tokyo?
- Is it too late to call my brother in Sydney?
- If it's nine here, what is it in New York?
- Is my mum awake in Lagos?
- Time over there now?

Ravi, a retired teacher, was playing his guitar on the porch when his old dog scratched at the door. 'I don't want him to eat before his walk,' Ravi told the pet feeder, 'so ask the bowl to stay closed until we are back.' The assistant locked the feeder lid and said it would open at six. 'Open it straight after the walk instead,' Ravi said. The assistant moved the feeding time to right after the walk and said it would open the lid when Ravi told it they were back. Ravi put the guitar down, clipped on the lead, and walked out slowly with his friend. When they returned, he said so, the lid clicked open, and the dog ate happily.

name: spare_key_code
does: Gives a visitor a temporary door code that stops working after the day you choose, so nobody needs a silly hidden key and you reduce the worry about lost keys.
inputs: who the code is for, and the day or days it should work
people say:
- My cleaner comes Saturday, give her a code for that day
- Let my friend in while I'm out, a code until tonight
- Make a one-time code for the delivery man
- I don't want to hide a key, set up a temporary code
- Guests arrive tomorrow, give them a code until Sunday

Watching a movie at home usually means a television, a phone or a laptop. People look for what is on tonight, watch a trailer, or find a film in a certain mood, like a comedy for the weekend. Before a long trip, some people download a movie so they can watch it without internet. Downloads take time, so you have to be patient. Cinemas have times for each show, and people check them before leaving the house. People say, 'What movies are on tonight?' 'Find a funny one for the kids,' 'Download this for the train,' or 'When does the next show start?'

Marisol had just moved to the city and wanted to know what was happening. She stood at the kitchen sink, where the tap dripped, and said, 'Give me today's local news, but I don't want sports or celebrity stories.' The assistant kept each headline short, and Marisol could hear it clearly over the dripping tap. The third headline said water on her street would be off from noon to four. She asked the assistant to remind her at eleven to fill a few bottles. It set the reminder and offered a short update after lunch. Marisol said yes.
